chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abul Azaqir al-Shalmaghani mentioned in the beginning of the Book of Occultation which he composed

As for the dispute between me and the mentioned man, may Allah increase his success, I have no right to interfere in it except for one whom I involve, because the injury is upon me, so I am the one entitled to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the basis for an Imam's or scholar's authority in resolving a personal dispute according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abul Azaqir clarifies the jurisdictional basis of his dispute, asserting that the right of retribution (*al-jarīna*) belongs to him as the aggrieved party. This highlights the Shia legal principle that the victim holds the authority to forgive or exact compensation, and can choose to delegate this right to others, reflecting the personal nature of certain civil rights in Imami jurisprudence.
